title: Signal retrospective: adaptive sampling + dashboard hygiene
content:
Context and purpose:
This doc captures the Observability team sync on 2026-05-06 and the mid-week followups. Primary focus: evaluate the first two weeks of adaptive sampling trials for traces, cleanup of dashboard duplicates, and a short cost-telemetry spike investigation. Intention is to leave a readable, operational narrative plus explicit action items and owners so anyone can pick these up next week.

Attendees:
- Aisha (owner)
- Marcus (tracing lead)
- Sofia (dashboards / UX)
- Diego (cost telemetry / billing)
- Janelle (sre liaison)

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Adaptive sampling experiment is reducing ingested span counts by ~38% for tail-heavy services (svc-rewrite, svc-search) with <3% impact on top-level latency SLI telemetry. Early signal: useful for cost savings, but sampling skew surfaced for error debugging in svc-search.
- Dashboard hygiene pass removed 12 near-duplicate panels across infra and app dashboards; consolidated per-route token-cost panel (requested by product) is live in the canary folder.
- Cost spike on 2026-05-04 traced to a scheduled batch job (analysis-runner) that switched to a higher parallelism after a platform deploy; caused extra queries and extra traced spans — billing impact ~2.7% of monthly hosted ingestion.
- Action items prioritized: refine sampling filter rules (Marcus), add synthetic error traces to the search stack to validate sampling (Janelle), and add cost alerting for non-API batch runs (Diego).

Detailed notes:
1) Adaptive sampling experiment updates (Marcus)
   - What we ran: per-service adaptive sampler (probabilistic with retention boosting for error spans + dynamic reservoir for new transactions). Deployed to svc-rewrite, svc-search, svc-ingest on 2026-04-22.
   - Metrics observed (week 1->2):
     * Ingested spans: svc-rewrite -43%, svc-search -36%, svc-ingest -18%
     * Error trace retention: nominally +2% (thanks to retention boosting)
     * Headroom: pipeline CPU usage down ~15% on collector machines
   - Issues found:
     * svc-search: specific error class (Timeout::ShardFetch) is sampled out in some cases because client-side retries produce many low-value spans. Lossy view made debugging a real incident harder.
     * Edge case: new feature flag flows (ff-payment-v2) had extremely low cardinality and got over-sampled into the reservoir, skewing retention away from production traffic.
   - Decisions / next steps:
     1) Add explicit rule to always keep spans with exception type Timeout::ShardFetch for svc-search for 30 days (Marcus) — Jira JIRA-OBS-981 assigned.
     2) Introduce a small windowed dedupe for immediate retries at the collector (reduce duplicate low-value spans) — spike by Marcus/Diego next sprint.
     3) Continue adaptive for svc-rewrite and svc-ingest; maintain canary on svc-search with tightened rules.

2) Dashboard cleanup & consolidation (Sofia)
   - Performed a manual audit across app and infra dashboards. Major themes:
     * Many panels are identical except for filter defaults (env=prod vs env=all).
     * Multiple cost-related panels were inconsistent in units (USD vs tokens/month).
   - Actions taken this week:
     * Removed 12 duplicate panels; moved 5 panels into a new folder: Observability/Canaries/Cost-and-Latency.
     * Built a canonical per-route token-cost panel that aggregates token + compute time and normalizes to USD using current pricing sheet (linked). Canary link: dashboards/canary/per-route-token-cost.
   - Follow-ups:
     * Sofia to run an audit script (small bash + grafana api) to find panels with same series but different templating (due 2026-05-13).
     * Add a short README inside the dashboard folder explaining canonical panels and where to add new ones (Sofia).

3) Cost telemetry spike (Diego)
   - Incident summary (2026-05-04 03:15 -> 03:58 UTC): upwards blip in traced span cost ingestion. Root cause: analysis-runner increased parallelism from 4->16 after deploy, more queries created, each query traced.
   - Quantified impact: additional spans ~4.2M, estimated extra monthly ingest if continuous: ~2.7% hosted ingestion cost. But this was short-lived.
   - Short-term mitigation: rolled back parallelism to 4, re-ran a few jobs after changing query planner flags.
   - Longer-term: Diego to add a policy that non-API batch jobs must be excluded from default trace retention (or have lower sampling) unless explicitly opted into full tracing. Implement policy as a checklist in infra-runbooks (Diego, due 2026-05-21).

4) SLOs and alerting (Janelle)
   - Observed: alert fatigue on a noisy 99th p99 latency alert; investigation shows many alerts originate from canary/experimental flows.
   - Plan:
     * Re-target p99 alert to exclude routes: /canary/* and dev-internal routes. Add a test that ensures new routes get flagged if they match canary pattern (Janelle).
     * Add a cost-telemetry alert that triggers when daily ingestion delta > 1.5x baseline for same service and job-type (Diego + Marcus). Threshold tuning to follow after 2 weeks of baseline data.

5) Observability playbook fragments (notes-to-self style)
   - Quick triage checklist for trace cost spikes:
     * Confirm scheduled jobs in last deploy window (check infra-scheduler, timestamped).
     * Check collector CPU/queue metrics for backpressure (collector-CPU > 70%?).
     * Look for cardinality explosions in span tags (user_id/session_id misuse).
     * If batch job identified, tag run with job-type=batch in traces and lower sampling for next run.
   - Debugging low-retention errors (svc-search example):
     * Reproduce failure in canary with synthetic workload (Janelle).
     * If error traces missing, enable a 100% retention override for a short time window and capture full trace.

Action items (explicit):
- Marcus: implement Timeout::ShardFetch retention rule for svc-search and open PR for config change (JIRA-OBS-981) — due 2026-05-10.
- Marcus/Diego: spike windowed dedupe for immediate retries at collector; small benchmark and RFC — due 2026-05-17.
- Sofia: audit script for duplicate panels and add README to canonical dashboard folder — due 2026-05-13.
- Diego: add policy + runbook entry for batch jobs default sampling; create alert for ingestion delta >1.5x — due 2026-05-21.
- Janelle: create canary with synthetic error workload for svc-search and run 3 experiments to validate sampling rule — due 2026-05-14.
- Aisha: write short post-mortem template for cost spikes that teams can reuse; circulate to platform-eng and product — due 2026-05-11.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- How do we balance reservoir allocation between low-cardinality new features vs high-volume core routes? Flags, quotas, or time-based cooling? (discussion required).
- Should we expose a simple UI in Console to opt certain job-types into full tracing? Risk: misuse by product teams leads to cost spikes. (product sync suggested).
- What SLA should we have for adjusting sampling rules after a production incident? Current process is ad-hoc and slow.

Misc notes / useful links:
- Quick link: dashboards/canary/per-route-token-cost (canary)
- Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/354 (adaptive sampler config)
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-981 (svc-search sampling rule), CON-OBS-1423 (dashboard cleanup tracker)
- Slack: #observability thread ts:1712345678.000200 — contains raw logs and heatmaps from the spike window.

Retro + items to try next sprint (thinking):
- Experiment: reservoir share that prioritizes spans by route importance (config file with weights per route) — small experiment on svc-ingest.
- Investigate cheap client-side dedupe library (JS + Python SDK) to cut duplicate retry spans before they hit collector (low lift?).
- Schedule a quarterly audit for dashboards and alerts ownership — rotate owners each quarter.

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep the narrative short for exec digest but keep the technical bits in this doc. Will produce a 1-paragraph exec summary for EOD Friday.
- Remind product to include "job-type" in telemetry schema for batch jobs — helps grouping and alerting.

End of notes.

-- Aisha (observability)
